title: A cascade of orbital-field-driven phases with a Lifshitz-type transition to unidirectional spiral order
abstract: Frustration in magnetic systems gives rise to unconventional orders and exotic spin liquids. Here, we explore a new type of frustration arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field that couples orbital degrees of freedom to spin correlations. Introducing this orbital-field interaction into the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, we show that local spin-orbital constraints generate a subextensive degeneracy, lifted by order-by-disorder to select distinct collinear magnets in a cascade of phases as the orbital field increases from a para-orbital liquid. At larger fields, the selected phase gives way to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral that spontaneously breaks chiral symmetry. This transition is driven by the coupling of a Goldstone mode to gapped dynamical spin-orbital fluctuations. The spin stiffness becomes negative along a particular direction, while the spiral wavevector grows as the square root of the distance from the transition, signaling a Lifshitz-type transition. We present a microscopic route to realizing this orbital field and discuss candidate materials.
summary: This work explores magnetic frustration in a honeycomb lattice model driven by an orbital-field interaction. The system exhibits a sequence of magnetic phases as the field strength increases, culminating in a transition to an incommensurate spiral state. This transition is characterized by a Lifshitz instability, providing a microscopic route to understanding complex magnetic ordering in correlated materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates a novel frustration mechanism arising from an intrinsic bond-dependent orbital-field coupling to spin correlations, leading to a cascade of magnetic phases and a Lifshitz-type transition.
main_result: The system undergoes a transition from a para-orbital liquid through collinear magnet phases to an incommensurate unidirectional spiral order, signaled by a Lifshitz instability where the spin stiffness vanishes along one direction.
method: The study employs variational methods on the Heisenberg model supplemented by an orbital-field interaction, analyzing quantum fluctuations via Linear Flavor-Wave theory to determine the true ground state.
model_or_system: The model is an antiferromagnetic Heisenberg model on the honeycomb lattice, incorporating orbital degrees of freedom ($	au$) via an orbital-field Hamiltonian ($\mathcal{H}_{	ext{orb}}$). The interactions are parameterized by the ratio $\kappa/J$.
key_observables: Spin correlations, spin stiffness ($ho_{\perp}$), spiral wavevector ($\mathbf{Q}_0$), and the relative zero-point energy of different dimer coverings.
important_parameters: The ratio $\kappa/J$ controls the phase transitions; critical points include $\kappa/J = 1/2$ and $\kappa_{c3}/J \simeq 3.303$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the system to effective low-energy Hamiltonians describing Goldstone modes coupled to gapped spin-orbital fluctuations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the lattice structure and orbital pseudospins, the semiclassical phase diagram showing the cascade of phases, and the LFW spectra demonstrating the softening and Lifshitz-type instability at the critical point.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the orbital-field frustrated model on the honeycomb lattice, analyzing the resulting subextensive degeneracy of collinear states, and finally detailing the quantum selection mechanism leading to the incommensurate spiral phase via a Lifshitz instability.
why_interesting: The mechanism of orbital-field coupling driving a Lifshitz transition is highly relevant to understanding exotic magnetic ordering in transition metal oxides, a key area in strongly correlated electron physics.
